slot.brief: A sample's activity drops to a given fraction after some time; ask how many half-lives elapsed, or find the time for activity to drop by a stated factor.

stem: The activity of a radioactive sample falls to $\dfrac{1}{32}$ of its initial value in $10$ h. The half-life of the sample is

verdicts.working: \(1/32=(1/2)^5\), so 10 h is five half-lives. The half-life is \(10/5=2\) h.

working:
$\dfrac{A}{A_0}=\left(\dfrac12\right)^n=\dfrac{1}{32}=\left(\dfrac12\right)^5$
$n=5,\qquad t_{1/2}=\dfrac{10\ \mathrm{h}}{5}=2\ \mathrm{h}$

Independent check: \(1/32=(1/2)^5\), so 10 h is five half-lives. The half-life is \(10/5=2\) h.
solution:
Activity after $n$ half-lives is $A/A_0=(1/2)^n$. Since $1/32=(1/2)^5$, the 10 h interval contains 5 half-lives.
$$t_{1/2}=\frac{10\ \mathrm{h}}{5}=2\ \mathrm{h}$$
